books.name: If and Since
books.focus: if · unless · too / enough · for / since

items.a: Hurry, or you'll miss the bus.
items.b: If you ___ up, you'll miss the bus.
items.tip: … or you'll… = If you don't…, you'll…
items.say: If you don't hurry up, you'll miss the bus.

items.a: The water was too cold for us to swim in.
items.b: The water wasn't ___ for us to swim in.
items.tip: too cold = not warm enough (enough goes after the adjective).
items.say: The water wasn't warm enough for us to swim in.

items.a: The box is so heavy that I can't lift it.
items.b: The box is ___ for me to lift.
items.tip: so heavy that I can't = too heavy for me to…
items.say: The box is too heavy for me to lift.

items.a: Unless you water the plant, it will die.
items.b: If you ___ the plant, it will die.
items.tip: unless = if … not: unless you water = if you don't water.
items.say: If you don't water the plant, it will die.

items.a: I haven't got a map, so I can't find the castle.
items.b: If I ___ a map, I could find the castle.
items.tip: Imagined situations now: If + past simple, … could/would: If I had a map…
items.say: If I had a map, I could find the castle.

items.a: Mia started learning judo three years ago.
items.b: Mia has ___ judo for three years.
items.tip: started … ago → has been learning … for (present perfect + for).
items.say: Mia has been learning judo for three years.

items.a: It's ages since I last saw my cousin.
items.b: I ___ my cousin for ages.
items.tip: It's ages since I last saw = I haven't seen … for ages.
items.say: I haven't seen my cousin for ages.

items.a: The last time I rode a horse was in May.
items.b: I ___ a horse since May.
items.tip: The last time … was in May = I haven't … since May. ride → ridden.
items.say: I haven't ridden a horse since May.

items.a: Someone stole my bike yesterday.
items.b: My bike ___ yesterday.
items.tip: Passive in the past: was/were + past participle: My bike was stolen.
items.say: My bike was stolen yesterday.

items.a: They built the castle in 1300.
items.b: The castle ___ in 1300.
items.tip: The castle is the thing the action happened to → passive: was built.
items.say: The castle was built in 1300.

items.a: When I was little, I often played with toy dinosaurs.
items.b: I ___ with toy dinosaurs when I was little.
items.tip: Past habits that have stopped: used to + verb.
items.say: I used to play with toy dinosaurs when I was little.

items.a: 'I am hungry,' said Leo.
items.b: Leo said that he ___ hungry.
items.tip: In reported speech the tense moves back: am → was.
items.say: Leo said that he was hungry.

items.a: 'Can you help me?' Ana asked me.
items.b: Ana asked me if I ___ help her.
items.tip: Reported questions: can → could, and no question order: asked if I could help.
items.say: Ana asked me if I could help her.

items.a: People speak English in many countries.
items.b: English ___ in many countries.
items.tip: Passive in the present: is/are + past participle: English is spoken.
items.say: English is spoken in many countries.

items.a: 'Don't touch the dragon egg!' the wizard told us.
items.b: The wizard told us ___ the dragon egg.
items.tip: Reported orders: told someone (not) to + verb: told us not to touch.
items.say: The wizard told us not to touch the dragon egg.

items.a: There was nobody in the classroom.
items.b: There ___ in the classroom.
items.tip: nobody = not … anybody: There wasn't anybody.
items.say: There wasn't anybody in the classroom.

books.name: Same Idea, New Words
books.focus: bored by · never been · far from · old enough

items.a: My favourite subject is art.
items.b: I like art ___ any other subject.
items.tip: favourite = the one you like more than any other.
items.say: I like art more than any other subject.

items.a: The film was boring.
items.b: I was ___ the film.
items.tip: -ing describes the thing (boring film); -ed describes how you feel (I was bored).
items.say: I was bored by the film.

items.a: How about going to the aquarium?
items.b: Why ___ go to the aquarium?
items.tip: How about …ing? = Why don't we…? / Why not…? (suggestions).
items.say: Why don't we go to the aquarium?

items.a: This is my first time on a plane.
items.b: I have ___ on a plane before.
items.tip: my first time = I have never … before.
items.say: I have never been on a plane before.

items.a: Is it OK if I use your pencil?
items.b: Do you mind ___ your pencil?
items.tip: Do you mind if I + verb? / Do you mind me using…? is a polite way to ask.
items.say: Do you mind if I use your pencil?

items.a: The museum is very near my house.
items.b: The museum isn't ___ my house.
items.tip: very near = not far from.
items.say: The museum isn't far from my house.

items.a: Tom is too young to drive.
items.b: Tom isn't ___ to drive.
items.tip: too young = not old enough.
items.say: Tom isn't old enough to drive.

items.a: Nobody in my class is as fast as Kemi.
items.b: Kemi is ___ person in my class.
items.tip: Nobody is as fast as Kemi = Kemi is the fastest.
items.say: Kemi is the fastest person in my class.
